You were going to say something about Pequil. Was Pequil like that?

Well, Pequil was a different man. Pequil would play music very suddenly. Yeah, you see, Pequil is a tinsmith. He's supposed to be a tinsmith, you understand? But he was such a nice man, he was like that big time. Then again, the little things about Pequil, Pequil was a whole lot jealous of his wife. And that made him make believe he was going to play music and hide around the house.
That was true. Yeah.

He had around the house, see what's going on. Then his wife was a midwife. Yeah, she was a fine woman. He was a tinsmith, you know what that man. Plenty of money. And then, that day, you know, the man makes three full hours a day, he was making money. Yeah. Yeah.
Did the, did you ever, you know, I mean, you must have heard Pequil, how was he in those days? Anything like he is right now? Is he about the same?
No, no, no, no, no. He was a pretty good man. Yeah?
Yeah, don't let nobody say that. He was a pretty good man. He was good. He still sounds good when I hear him play.

Yeah, he's a pretty good man and he's a pretty good musician too. Yeah, he's a good musician. But now, what I'm saying is he's 80 years old or something now. Yeah, well that shows you what it's all about. He's still playing.
In fact, he must love music or he wouldn't get it out of a play like you say. You've got to love music.

Yeah, he's just a little bit of an island. He'd have work there and all. Well, myself, I used to do that. I used to have 15 or 20 mattresses to go out. People would sleep on the floor. I'd go out for a job, down a half job, I'd leave 10 or 15 hours in it. And what I'd do? We'd stop in the island, I'd spend that up and go in the park and get some more. Let that go. No, no. And everywhere I went, it was that same thing. That's what I tell any man, I'm thankful. I went everywhere and my places where there wasn't no good. And I got in, they come out there, it's just like I went in, I put no kind of blunder, whatever. No hard word or nothing now. Everybody said, one boy, one boy, one boy, one boy, one boy. That's true.
Well, where was your mattress shop or factory, whatever you call it in the old days? Where did you make your mattresses?

Well, in the old days I was on the Maroney and Whitewater. Yeah, I had a 90 night court, that was my place there. I had lots of work there. Had a whole house covered. Had a whole, you had some people come up, came up one night there. Then I worked, like the condon, well I worked at home condon. I worked at home.

I remember once, about 1943, 17 years ago when I wanted to see Maurice Durand, he worked at a mattress factory too. It was down in that section someplace, about Maroney. That wouldn't be the same place. Do you remember where he worked? No, no, no.
Yeah, yeah, he worked down here on Charter and Cluett.
Oh yeah.
Yeah, Charter, most of the river. Yeah, that's where he was.
That wasn't your place then, you were alone in there. No, no, no, no.
I was up here on the, on the Maroney and Whitewater. Yeah.
Yeah, he was downtown farther, I forgot where it was. What did you use in those days? Somebody said you used Spanish moss in your mattresses and the deal, or what other?

They called it Spanish moss, but I didn't say we always used exultant, what they call exultant, what they used to use on the ships. You see that? The ship they use an exultant, what you call a cotton top. Exultant in the cotton top here. And when that mattress crushed, all they done throw it away in all the new mattresses. Okay. And the public would use what you call moss. You see? Because the moss mattress, all you done with that, then when you renovate that, you could use the old ticking, the same ticking. And if you wanted a new ticking, you would apply a new ticking to that. You see? But if it was too heavy, you wouldn't add any moss to it. But if you wanted it heavier, you would add moss to it. And that was it. Then you had the old box spring mattresses. You see? That was different from the one they use now. You see, most of the French people would call it, how do you call it, spring some air. See? That thing would take two good minutes to handle that. Yeah. Yeah. It's heavy waste. Put up a rock with some with pine wood and some with cypress wood. Like they got them now, they're easy. But they're not as long as you get some of those mattresses. In them days, 10, 15, 20 years, the ticking had to wear out for an inch ago. Yeah. Yeah, the ticking had to wear out. You could do what you want. All you got is preserve the ticking and stop it from getting dirty. If you've done that, you see.
Yeah. My mother, who has a bad back, got a hair mattress a few years ago. What do they put in those? Is it really some kind of hair? Do you know what a hair mattress is?
Well, that's a hair. Yeah, that's a hair.
Like horse hair or something? Or what kind of hair do they use?
Well, I was always learned about this, which I don't know if it's right or wrong. That's the hair that comes from the sea.
Something…
Comes from the sea.
Yeah, it isn't from animals.

No, it's not an animal hair. An animal hair would be short. Yeah, that's right. You know what I'm saying? But if it's a hair, you can grab it a handful like that and you wouldn't have a pound. You see, the heavier than those mattresses, you take for instance, like a 40 or 45 pounds of that hair, eating that, and you look at it, you'd say, oh man, that's too much. How are you going to handle that? You understand? It's puffed up like that. That's the whole mattress. You understand? You know what I'm saying? Because that hair now, the most of my work was not done to hair mattress, the people would recommend me to the house. We didn't clean that mattress with the machine. See? Take that stuff and take about four tubs. You understand? Like in them times we had the grandma powder. Grandma powder in here and each one of the tub. You get that tub, you put it there, you sop it, and you sop it, and you shake it, and you chew it to the other tub, and you sop it. Just keep on until you've got the soup out of it. And you spread it around like on the lawn, a good clean place there where the sun hit it. And finally, a tongue, a spring like that, yeah. Now that's going to stay there four or five years before it packs, or maybe longer. Maybe longer, yeah. Now that's a mattress they used to use on the seas. Like those big ships driving, they used to use them. Why? Because you can take about 15 or 18 pounds, maybe 20 pounds, and you had a single bed. It was light, a single bed. Until after the other mattresses come along though. The wind mattresses, they cut that out.
